mainEntity.name: Why is there a dark line visible at the edge of my veneer?

acceptedAnswer.text: A visible dark or grey line at the edge of a veneer near the gumline is a relatively common concern and can have several causes. It may indicate that the gum has receded slightly, exposing the margin area that was previously hidden. In some cases, it may reflect discolouration of the bonding cement used to secure the veneer. In others, it may suggest the underlying tooth structure is showing through. A dental assessment can identify the precise cause and discuss whether any treatment is appropriate for your individual situation.

mainEntity.name: How long do veneer margins typically last before they need attention?

acceptedAnswer.text: Veneer longevity varies considerably depending on the quality of the original placement, the materials used, how well the patient maintains their oral hygiene, and lifestyle factors such as teeth grinding or dietary habits. High-quality porcelain veneers placed by an experienced clinician and cared for well can last ten to fifteen years or longer. Margins may require assessment or attention earlier than this if there is significant gum recession, bite changes, or marginal wear. Regular check-ups allow any changes to be identified and managed at an early stage.

mainEntity.name: Can veneer margins be repaired without replacing the veneer entirely?

acceptedAnswer.text: In some circumstances, minor margin issues — such as small chips, slight roughness, or surface staining at the edge — can be addressed through polishing, recontouring, or bonding without the need for full veneer replacement. However, this depends entirely on the nature and extent of the marginal problem. If the veneer itself has structurally failed, the margin is significantly broken, or the veneer no longer fits the tooth correctly, replacement may be the more appropriate solution. Only a clinical examination can determine which approach is suitable. You may also find it useful to read about why marginal fit matters for veneers.

mainEntity.name: Can poorly fitting veneer margins cause gum problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, there is a known relationship between margin quality and gum health. When a veneer margin has an open gap, overhangs slightly, or sits in an area that is difficult to clean, plaque and bacteria can accumulate in that area. Over time, this can lead to localised gum inflammation, redness, or bleeding. If left unaddressed, ongoing marginal irritation may contribute to gum recession or bone changes around the affected tooth. Maintaining excellent oral hygiene around veneer margins and attending regular dental check-ups helps minimise this risk.

mainEntity.name: Does grinding my teeth affect veneer margins?

acceptedAnswer.text: Teeth grinding (bruxism) can place significant stress on the thin edges of veneers, making margins more susceptible to chipping, fracturing, or debonding over time. The margins, being the thinnest part of the veneer, are particularly vulnerable to repeated mechanical loading. Patients who grind their teeth and have veneers are often advised to wear a custom-fitted night guard to protect the restorations during sleep. It is important to discuss any history of grinding with your dentist before veneer treatment is planned, as this will influence the preparation design and material selection. For related risk factors, see this overview on whether porcelain veneers can crack over time.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my veneers still fit correctly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Regular dental check-ups are the most reliable way to monitor the fit and condition of your veneers. Your dentist can use clinical probing and visual examination to assess whether the margins remain well-sealed, check for any gum changes around the veneer edges, and evaluate the bite. If you notice changes between appointments — such as new sensitivity, a different feeling when you bite, rough edges, or visible changes to the gum around a veneered tooth — it is sensible to arrange a review rather than wait for your next routine appointment.
